coord_notes.kind: The extension adds one row \(v\) to the embedding table, i.e. one new input symbol \(S_*\). On the original input space \(X\) every \(v\) is neutral, since no prompt without \(S_*\) reads the row. So on \(X\) the method is the frozen model, and its whole effect lives on the enlarged input space \(X^+\supset X\).
coord_notes.shape: Affine in \(v\): \(E^+=[E_0;\,v]\), with \(d=d_{\rm emb}\) (\(kd\) for a \(k\)-vector pseudo-word). Linear in the extended weight space \(\Theta^+\); function-level relative to \(\Theta\), which has no row for \(S_*\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(v_0=E_w\) for a coarse descriptor \(w\) ('cat'). Then \(\tilde f(\theta_0,v_0,-)=f(\theta_0,-)\circ(S_*\mapsto w)\), so the extension is pointed relative to substituting \(w\) for \(S_*\).
coord_notes.gauge: \(v\mapsto[E_0;v]\) is injective.
coord_notes.covariance: As for Trainable Tokens: the row is a free vector on the embedding side (\(GL\)); on the vocabulary side only token-preserving (monomial) maps are allowed.
coord_notes.merge: The learned row is an ordinary embedding entry, so inference cost is unchanged: M1 into its own box. It cannot be merged into \(\Theta\) itself only because \(f\) has no input \(S_*\). That is a change of input type, not an M∞ obstruction.

methods.categorical_reading: Textual inversion is a pointed extension of the input alphabet rather than of the network. It adjoins one symbol \(S_*\) whose embedding is a free point \(v\in\mathbb R^d\), neutral at \(v_0=E_w\) via the substitution \(S_*\mapsto w\). On the old inputs it is the initial object (Frozen). On prompts containing \(S_*\) it is Trainable Tokens on the extended table, the Lin row method of \(\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta^+,\theta_0^+)\).

arrows.note: Trainable Tokens on the extended vocabulary with \(T=\{S_*\}\), pointed at the descriptor row \(E_w\). This is HF PEFT's TrainableTokensConfig on a newly added token after resize_token_embeddings.
Freezing Custom Diffusion's cross-attention \(W^k,W^v\) at \(W_0\) leaves its modifier-token row. The target is Custom Diffusion pointed at \((0,0,E_w)\) rather than at its rare-token init.

obstructions.reason: Textual inversion is pointed: \(v_0=E_w\) reproduces the prompt with the word \(w\). A soft prompt always draws attention mass, and on a head with \(W_oW_v\ne0\) it has no neutral value (Thm VI.5(f)). The base-point strata differ, so there is no pointed arrow either way.

coord_notes.kind: Two summands. One is a selective block: dense \(W^k,W^v\) in every cross-attention layer, an R part. The other is a new modifier-token row \(V^*\), a vocabulary extension as in Textual Inversion. The extension makes the whole object E: an extension followed by a reparametrisation of \(\Theta\times\mathbb R^{d_{\rm text}}\).
coord_notes.shape: Affine: a coordinate block of the extended weight space, of dimension \(2d_{\rm out}d_{\rm text}\) per cross-attention layer plus \(d_{\rm text}\) for \(V^*\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\Delta W=0\), and \(V^*_0\) is a rare token's embedding. The model is unchanged on ordinary prompts and treats \(V^*\) as that rare token.
coord_notes.gauge: A coordinate inclusion: injective.
coord_notes.covariance: Each selected box is fully trainable (\(GL\times GL\)). The modifier row is Mon×GL on the vocabulary side, as for Textual Inversion.
coord_notes.merge: The fine-tuned \(W^k,W^v\) replace the originals and \(V^*\) is one vocabulary row. The closed-form multi-concept merge is a separate post-hoc operation, a constrained least squares of RegMean type.

methods.categorical_reading: Custom Diffusion is Textual Inversion \(\oplus\) a selective block. The block is surgical fine-tuning of exactly the boxes that read the text wire (\(W^k,W^v\)), plus one adjoined vocabulary symbol. Its multi-concept merge is a P operation \(\Theta^N\to\Theta\). It solves a least-squares problem under hard equality constraints on the concepts' features, so it is a constrained RegMean rather than task arithmetic.

obstructions.reason: Dense \(W^k,W^v\) updates reach rank \(\min(d_{\rm out},d_{\rm text})>r\). The paper finds low-rank training worse; only post-hoc SVD compression comes close.
SVDiff keeps \(W_0\)'s singular frames, an absolute invariant; dense K/V updates move them.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: E (selective K/V block plus an adjoined vocabulary row), Lin, neutral, none, M1, idempotent agree. Covariance is a product of box groups (GLxGL on W^k, W^v; MonxGL on the V* row); GLxGL labels the principal boxes and the note records the row, so kept. O2 to LoRA (dense rank > r) and O1 to SVDiff (frames move) valid. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: The selected routed experts are fine-tuned in place. Router, attention, shared experts and embeddings stay frozen.
coord_notes.shape: A coordinate subspace: the full weights of the selected experts \(E_s^l\) in each layer, \(d=\sum_l|E_s^l|\cdot3dd_{ff}^{(e)}\).
coord_notes.covariance: Each selected expert is fully trainable box by box (\(GL\times GL\)). Experts are blocks the MoE already has, so no partition is imposed. The selection is a data statistic of the frozen router, which every function-preserving reparametrisation carries along.
coord_notes.rebasing: Fixed expert set: idempotent. Recomputing relevance scores after a merge could change the set and gain.

methods.categorical_reading: ESFT is surgical fine-tuning indexed by experts instead of layers: the trainable set is a union of whole expert boxes, chosen from router statistics on task data. Like surgical FT and Spectrum, it is a Lin, regular, idempotent coordinate block. Only the selection rule (routing mass) is new.

obstructions.reason: Each selected expert gets a dense update of rank up to \(\min(d,d_{ff}^{(e)})>r\).

ESFT trains a few experts in every MoE layer at once, on a fixed support. A LISA stage trains only \(\gamma\) sampled layers (all experts in them) plus embeddings and head. So, when \(\gamma\) is below the number of MoE layers, no single stage contains ESFT's image. (That ESFT never touches the embeddings blocks only the converse LISA \(\to\) ESFT.)

methods.check_notes: Re-derived R / Lin / regular / none / GLxGL (router statistics are function-level, carried by box-wise function-preserving gauges) / M1 / idempotent; agree. O2 to LoRA valid. Change: LISA obstruction reason now states the gamma < #MoE-layers condition and moves the 'never touches the embeddings' remark to the converse direction, where it belongs.

coord_notes.kind: Training-free: an endomorphism of the space of trained LoRA adapters. The catalog files it as a training procedure, but it is post hoc.
coord_notes.shape: With \(W_1=W_0+\Delta W\), the \(\lambda\)-family \(\lambda\mapsto W_1+(\lambda-1)\sum_{j\in\mathcal I}\sigma_ju_jv_j^\top\) rescales the intruder singular values of \(W_1\) along fixed singular vectors. It is affine in \(\lambda\) (the closure of a one-parameter torus orbit). Since a single \(\lambda\) (HF mitigation_lambda) is shared by every adapted matrix, \(d=1\) for the whole model, not per matrix. HF's rank-\(r\) re-factorisation makes it smooth but not affine near \(\lambda=1\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\lambda=1\) returns the trained adapter, so relative to \(\theta_0\) the family carries the defect \(e=\Delta W\) by design. In the slice at \(W_1\) it is regular. No \(\lambda\) returns \(\theta_0\) unless \(\Delta W\) lies in the intruder span.
coord_notes.gauge: Injective in \(\lambda\) once an intruder is detected. The rule reads only \(W_0+sBA\), so it is constant on LoRA's \(GL_r\) fibres: gauge-invariant (Prop V.4(a)), unlike factor-wise rules.
coord_notes.covariance: Intruders are detected by \(|\langle u_j,u^0_i\rangle|\) between the left singular frames of \(W_1\) and \(W_0\): \(CO\times CO\).
coord_notes.merge: The output is again a LoRA adapter.
coord_notes.rebasing: Applying the rule again to \(W'\) finds the same singular vectors with values \(\lambda\sigma_j\). The family is a multiplicative monoid on fixed directions, hence idempotent (until an intruder drops out of the top \(k\)).

methods.categorical_reading: A post-hoc spectral operation on the image of \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\). A one-parameter torus acts on those singular values of the merged weight whose left singular vectors are nearly orthogonal to \(W_0\)'s. In other words it is SVDiff re-based at the trained point and restricted to the intruder directions. It reads only the product \(BA\), so it descends to adapters (Prop V.4(a)).

arrows.note: Into SVDiff re-based at \(W_1=W_0+\Delta W\) (its SVD frame), with \(\lambda=1\) sent to \(\delta=0\). Paper variant (no rank-\(r\) re-truncation), \(\lambda\ge0\).

obstructions.reason: WiSE-FT moves along \(W_0+\alpha\Delta W\), shrinking the whole update toward \(\theta_0\). Intruder reduction moves along \(W_1+(\lambda-1)\sigma_ju_jv_j^\top\). The two lines meet only at \(W_1\), unless \(\Delta W\) is itself the intruder component.

A3 to SVDiff re-based at W_1 verified (pointed lambda=1 -> delta=0; needs lambda>=0 for the ReLU). O1 to WiSE-FT valid (two lines through W_1). Change: shape note d=1 'per matrix' -> d=1 for the whole model (lambda is global).

coord_notes.kind: \(F_X\): the prefix \(p(x)=\sum_m\alpha_m(x)P_m\) is a family over inputs, with weights read from a separate frozen forward pass.
coord_notes.shape: Function-level: for each \(x\), a prefix in the span of the components at layers 1–5.
coord_notes.base_point: Prefix slots always draw softmax mass, even for \(p=0\): zero keys have logit 0.
coord_notes.gauge: \(\alpha_m=\cos(q\odot A_m,K_m)\) is invariant under positive rescalings of \(A_m\) and of \(K_m\), and under a joint sign flip: a torus of dimension \(2M\). \(P_m\) has no slide, since \(\alpha_m\) is not a parameter.
coord_notes.covariance: The Hadamard feature gate \(q\odot A_m\) on the frozen query wire commutes only with monomial changes of basis there. The prefix components are free vectors on the key/value wire (\(GL\)).
coord_notes.merge: Input-dependent prefix slots lengthen the key/value sequence (Thm VI.5(f)).
coord_notes.rebasing: Nothing merges. Continual learning grows the component set instead, with earlier components frozen. That is an increasing chain of objects, not a rebasing.

methods.categorical_reading: CODA-Prompt is a continuous family over inputs, \(x\mapsto\sum_m\alpha_m(x)P_m\), of points of prefix tuning, with unnormalised cosine weights read from a frozen query pass. Each task adds components and freezes the earlier ones at their trained values. That freezing, not any property of the image, is how it limits forgetting.

obstructions.reason: CODA's prompt varies continuously with \(x\), while L2P's is piecewise constant (hard top-\(N\) retrieval). So generic CODA realisations are not L2P realisations.
A static prefix is a single point. CODA's prefix depends on \(x\) through \(q(x)\), so its realisations are generically not those of any single prefix.

coord_notes.kind: The transported object is an ordinary target-side LoRA (or DoRA, or soft prompt) trained by distillation. The source pair and the discriminator are training data, not part of \(\rho\).
coord_notes.base_point: Target LoRA at \(B=0\): the \(\mathrm T_A\) apex of \(\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta_t,\theta_t)\).

methods.categorical_reading: Trans-LoRA moves an adapter to a new base model that has no weight correspondence with the old one, so no base-change functor \(\phi_!\) exists. Instead it lifts the source realisation \(\Phi_{f_s}(\theta_s+\Delta_s)\) along the target realisation \(\Phi_{f_t}\circ\rho_{\rm LoRA}\), by distillation on synthetic inputs. The output is an object of the target slice, which is why the PEFT type may change in transit.

arrows.note: The same object on the target base. The distillation loss and the synthetic data are trained-method data.

obstructions.reason: The target is the full rank-\(r\) cone, \(d=r(m+n-r)\). LoRA-X's target is confined to frozen singular subspaces, with \(d=r\) (or \(r^2\)). So a Trans-LoRA output is generically not a LoRA-X point.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: the transported object is the target LoRA (R / Cone / apex T_A / GL / GLxGL / M1 / span); agree. A3 h=id to LoRA is an isomorphism on the target slice. O2 to LoRA-X valid: r(m+n-r) > r (or r^2). recipe entry type sensible. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Training uses \(W_0+\tilde U_r\Delta\Sigma\tilde V_r^\top\) with frozen top-\(r\) SVD frames. Transfer is a separate, training-free map between slices.
coord_notes.shape: Diagonal \(\Delta\Sigma\): \(W_0+U_r\mathrm{diag}(\mathbb R^r)V_r^\top\), the closure of the torus orbit on the top-\(r\) singular values, \(d=r\). The constraint \(\sigma_i+\delta\sigma_i\ge0\) keeps \(\theta_0\) an interior point. Full core: \(d=r^2\), the image of LoRA-XS.
coord_notes.base_point: \(\Delta\Sigma=0\) is inferred; the paper does not state the init.
coord_notes.gauge: Injective (diagonal or full core).
coord_notes.covariance: Truncated SVD frames: \(CO\times CO\) (Prop II.16).
coord_notes.rebasing: With the top-\(r\) frames frozen: idempotent (a diagonal in \(W_0\)'s own frame keeps the frames). Recomputing the SVD after a merge keeps the same singular vectors, but if a shifted value \(\sigma_i+\delta\sigma_i\) drops below \(\sigma_{r+1}\) the top-\(r\) set changes and a new direction becomes trainable, so recomputation can gain (up to the full-frame torus \(U\mathrm{diag}(\mathbb R^{\min})V^\top\)).

methods.categorical_reading: Diagonal LoRA-X is the torus acting on the top-\(r\) singular values of \(W_0\), i.e. SVDiff truncated to rank \(r\); its full-core variant is LoRA-XS. The transfer \(\Delta W\mapsto U_tU_t^\top\Delta W\,V_tV_t^\top\) is a two-sided orthogonal projection between slices at different base points \(\theta_s\to\theta_t\), not an arrow. With a thin SVD it is the identity on full-rank square layers (catalog caveat).

arrows.note: Freeze SVDiff's shifts for \(i>r\) at 0. On the constraint set \(\sigma_i+\delta\sigma_i\ge0\) the ReLU is the identity.
SVFT with the plain (diagonal) pattern pointed at \(M=0\), its tail \(i>r\) frozen. SVFT's official init is a small defect.
LoRA-XS in the form \(W_0+U_rR\,\Sigma_rV_r^\top\), pointed at \(R=0\) (needs \(\sigma_r>0\)). An isomorphism for the full-core variant.
Into LoRA pointed at \((U_r,0)\), the \(\mathrm T_B\) stratum.

coord_notes.kind: Step 2 is an input-independent translation \(z\mapsto z+v\) of selected head outputs, which enter \(W^O\) linearly. By Thm VI.3(a) it equals the bias edit \(\Delta b_O=\sum_{i\in T_l}W^O_{(i)}v_l^i\), so it reads as a weight-space method on the affine closure of \(o\_proj\) (the Table VIII.B convention for SSF and RED). Step 1, the \(L_1\)-penalised scaling probe, only chooses the support and is then discarded.
coord_notes.shape: Linear: \(\{\sum_{i\in T}W^O_{(i)}v_i\}\), \(d=Kd_{head}\).
coord_notes.base_point: The exactly pointed variant \(v=0\) is regular. The official init \(v\sim\mathcal N(0,10^{-6})\) leaves a negligible defect (the \(\approx\) convention of Table VIII.B).
coord_notes.gauge: Injective when the selected head blocks of \(W^O\) have independent columns (\(|T_l|d_{head}\le d\), generic).
coord_notes.covariance: As for BitFit, the offsets are free vectors on each selected head's wire. The support is a set of whole heads, a partition the attention already has, and the per-head \(W_V\)–\(W_O\) gauge carries the image to itself. So no structure is imposed.
coord_notes.merge: M1→ into \(o\_proj\)'s bias, by R1 through the linear \(W^O\). Llama and Gemma \(o\_proj\) have no bias slot, so one bias vector per edited layer must be added.

methods.categorical_reading: LoFiT is BitFit on the attention-output bias, restricted to a learned sparse set of heads. It is a Lin method whose image \(\sum_{i\in T}W^O_{(i)}\mathbb R^{d_{head}}\) lies inside the bias space. Its localisation step is an (IA)\(^3\)-type scaling probe, used only to choose the support.

arrows.note: Into BitFit on a model with \(o\_proj\) biases, pointed at 0. The image is a proper subspace of the \(o\_proj\) bias space.

obstructions.reason: LoReFT edits the residual stream only at selected positions (M∞); LoFiT shifts head outputs at every position. A position-uniform shift lies outside LoReFT's realisations, and conversely.

coord_notes.shape: \(\{BMA\}=\mathcal M_{\le r}\): exactly LoRA's cone. The mixer changes the parametrisation, not the image.
coord_notes.base_point: \(B_0=0\) with \(M_0,A_0\) random, so \(S_1=\{XM_0A_0\}\) has dimension \(mr\) when \(M_0\) is invertible. The deficit is \(r(n-r)\), as for LoRA.
coord_notes.gauge: \((B,M,A)\sim(BG,G^{-1}MH,H^{-1}A)\): \(GL_r\times GL_r\). The generic fibre dimension is \(|Q|-d=r(m+n)+r^2-r(m+n-r)=2r^2\).

methods.categorical_reading: MoSLoRA is LoRA with a gauge-enlarging middle factor. \(\rho(B,M,A)=W_0+sBMA\) factors through LoRA by \(h=(BM,A)\), and LoRA factors back through it by freezing \(M\). The two simulate each other with the same image and the same \(S_1\), but they are not isomorphic (\(|Q|\) differs by \(r^2\)). Any gain is therefore in the cometric \(K=D\rho\,\Lambda\,D\rho^\top\), not in expressivity.

The same three-factor form on 2-D weights, but FLoRA is pointed at \(h(q_0)=(0,M_0,A_0)\) rather than at its zero-core init.

coord_notes.kind: Each searched subnet is LoRA (on \(W_q,W_k\)) \(\oplus\) a serial bottleneck adapter \(\oplus\) VPT-Deep tokens, each truncated in depth and width. The VPT summand has no neutral value, so the sum is unpointed (as for UniPELT and MAM).
coord_notes.shape: Function-level: the adapter and prompt parts live on extensions, so the object is not a \(\oplus\)-word of \(\mathsf{Meth}\).
coord_notes.base_point: VPT tokens always draw attention. The official adapter is Xavier-initialised on both projections, so even the adapter starts off its neutral point \(U=0\).
coord_notes.gauge: LoRA's \(GL_r\) on its summand; the adapter and the prompts add only discrete symmetries.
coord_notes.covariance: All parts are dense: basis-free.
coord_notes.merge: Only the LoRA part fuses (M1). Adapter and prompts remain unless the search sets their depth to 0.

methods.categorical_reading: NOAH searches the truncations of one supernet \(\mathrm{LoRA}\oplus\mathrm{Adapter}\oplus\mathrm{VPT}\). For LoRA and adapter widths, a prefix slice is an A2 sub-object (freeze the trailing coordinates at 0). For VPT it is not: dropping a token is not freezing it at a base value, because a zero token still draws attention mass. The candidates therefore form a lattice of sub-objects only along the LoRA and adapter axes, and the chosen object is an unpointed extension.

obstructions.reason: Every GLoRA path is a weight-space reparametrisation (M1), so its realisations lie in \(\Phi_f(\Theta)\). NOAH's VPT tokens and non-linear adapter leave that set (Thm VI.3(c), VI.5(f)).

NOAH's LoRA on \(W_q,W_k\) changes every token's queries and keys. AutoPEFT has no module there: its adapters sit at the FFN and its prefixes only add key/value slots, so neither reproduces a generic low-rank change of the attention logits. (The VPT-Deep part alone would not obstruct, since a deep prompt acts at its layer as a constrained K/V prefix; the LoRA summand does.)

coord_notes.kind: Each configuration is serial adapter \(\oplus\) parallel adapter \(\oplus\) K/V prefix on a layer mask. Any nonzero prefix length leaves no neutral point.
coord_notes.shape: Function-level (non-linear adapters and prefixes).
coord_notes.base_point: AdapterHub adapters start near \(U=0\), but prefixes always draw attention mass. Only configurations with \(L_{PT}=0\) are pointed (neutral).
coord_notes.gauge: ReLU bottlenecks: the positive per-unit torus (R3) times permutations. The prefix adds nothing continuous.
coord_notes.covariance: Dense modules: basis-free.
coord_notes.merge: ReLU adapters and prefix slots are generically non-affine in the box input (Thm VI.3(c), VI.5(f)).

methods.categorical_reading: AutoPEFT optimises over a finite grid of objects \(\mathrm{SA}_{D_{SA}}\oplus\mathrm{PA}_{D_{PA}}\oplus\mathrm{Prefix}_{L_{PT}}\) on a layer mask and returns a Pareto front in (performance, budget \(|M|\)). Size 0 removes a module, so the grid contains Pfeiffer-adapter, parallel-adapter and prefix-tuning objects as faces. The base-point type of a configuration jumps from neutral to unpointed as soon as \(L_{PT}>0\).

obstructions.reason: AutoPEFT's serial post-FFN adapter reads \(F(x)\), and a generic ReLU function of \(F(x)\) is not reproduced by MAM's parallel FFN adapter (which reads \(x\)) plus a key/value prefix (as for UniPELT vs MAM). Separately, the converse also fails: MAM's sizes (prefix length 30, fixed scaling) are not points of AutoPEFT's grid.
ReLU adapters and prefixes are non-affine inserted boxes (Thm VI.3(c)); no weight of the original architecture realises them.

methods.categorical_reading: EFT reads fine-tuning as a KL-regularised RL update, so a fine-tuned model is its base times \(\exp(r)\). It transports the implicit reward \(r\) from scale \(M\) to scale \(N\) in log-probability space. The per-token rule is Proxy-tuning's. EFT's derivation explains why the transport is meaningful: \(r\) is a base-independent, additive object in log space, as LoRA updates are in weight space.

methods.categorical_reading: WiSE-FT is task arithmetic with one task vector and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\): the segment from the zero-shot point to the fine-tuned point. When only the head is tuned, the segment is also an output ensemble, because \(f\) is linear in the head. Otherwise its success rests on linear mode connectivity, a property of \(\Phi_f\) along the segment rather than of the object.

methods.categorical_reading: Linear probing is the smallest non-trivial selective object: the head block alone. It is a linear sub-object of every method that also trains the head (A2, by freezing everything else). It is convex in \(V\), and the backbone factor stays at its base value, so the features are an absolute invariant.

methods.categorical_reading: LP-FT does not change the object: its second stage is Full FT, the terminal object, with image \(\Theta\). What changes is the base point on the head factor, \((v_0,B_0)\to(v_{\rm lp},B_0)\). The theory's head-alignment error \(\varphi^2\) is a function of that base point, so the gain is a purely dynamical (Exposé III) effect that the image invariants cannot see.

coord_notes.kind: Each round, clients train fresh LoRAs (ranks \(r_k\), \(B=0\)), the server stacks the factors, and every client merges \(W_0\leftarrow W_0+BA\). This is a merge-and-restart scheme: ReLoRA across clients.
coord_notes.shape: Per round the aggregate is \(\sum_kp_kB_kA_k\in\mathcal M_{\le\sum r_k}\): a cone at the current base.
coord_notes.base_point: Each round restarts at the apex (\(B_k=0\)).
coord_notes.gauge: \(\prod_kGL_{r_k}\) per round. Stacking acts on products, so the aggregation is gauge-invariant (Prop V.4(a)).
coord_notes.rebasing: A rebasing scheme: \(R_K=W_0+\mathcal M_{\le\min(K\sum_k r_k,m,n)}\) (Thm V.3, Cor 1).

methods.categorical_reading: FLoRA is a federated ReLoRA. Each round is the \(\oplus\) of the clients' LoRAs, \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathrm{LoRA}_{r_K}\cong\mathrm{LoRA}_{\sum r_k}\) by concatenation (Obs I.7), merged into the base before the next round. Stacking aggregates products, so it is exact and gauge-invariant, and heterogeneous ranks cost nothing. Its server step alone, with the client modules frozen, is the point \(\alpha=p\) of CAT's coefficient family; that is a point of LoRA soups, not an arrow from FLoRA's object, whose factors are trainable.

arrows.note: Stagewise into ReLoRA of rank \(\sum_kr_k\), pointed at the stacked \(A_0\)'s; the pointing is standard iff their rows are independent.

obstructions.reason: HetLoRA's zero-padded factor average has rank \(\le r_{\max}\); FLoRA's stacked aggregate reaches rank \(\sum_kr_k\).

coord_notes.kind: The global object is one \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r_{\max}}\) pair \((\bar B,\bar A)\), kept across rounds; clients train its leading-\(r_k\) truncations. The federation is a training procedure on this object.
coord_notes.base_point: Assumes LoRA's \(B=0\); the paper does not state the global init.
coord_notes.gauge: \(\rho\) has \(GL_{r_{\max}}\) fibres. Truncation to leading columns, however, is defined only up to the block-diagonal (Levi) subgroup of the flag \(\mathbb R^{r_{(1)}}\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb R^{r_{\max}}\) of client ranks. Averaging factors separately is bilinear (Prop V.4(b)), so the procedure is not a function of the adapters.

methods.categorical_reading: HetLoRA trains one \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r_{\max}}\) through a filtration of truncations, as DyLoRA does, except that the truncation levels are the clients' ranks rather than sampled ones. Its aggregation \((\sum p_kB_k)(\sum p_kA_k)\) acts on factors, so it carries LoRA's bilinearity error even in a fixed gauge. FLoRA (stacking) and FFA-LoRA (frozen \(A\)) are the two exact repairs of Prop V.4(b).

arrows.note: The global pair is a \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r_{\max}}\) point.
The same nested object, the truncation filtration of \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r_{\max}}\), with levels set by client capacity instead of sampled.

coord_notes.kind: In the default protocol the lite residual branches are part of the pretrained architecture. TinyTL therefore trains a coordinate block (all biases, the lite-residual weights and the head) of that network. With randomly initialised lite residuals (TinyTL-RandomL+B) it would be an extension without an exact neutral point.
coord_notes.shape: A coordinate subspace: biases \(\cup\) lite-residual group convolutions \(\cup\) head.
coord_notes.covariance: The trainable block itself is basis-free (each selected box fully trainable within its architectural class; the group convolutions are the network's own structure). But the frozen boxes sit on the 8-bit quantisation grid, which commutes only with monomial changes of basis: Mon x Mon (grid), as for QLoRA.
coord_notes.merge: Biases fold into their full-precision bias slots and nothing is added to a quantised box, so the grid is not left: M1 (not Mq). Nothing new at inference relative to the pretrained lite-residual network. Relative to a plain MobileNet, the lite branches would be non-linear extras (M∞).
coord_notes.base_point: The paper applies 8-bit weight quantisation to the frozen weights during transfer (Sec. 4, Training Details; the catalog's 'W frozen (8-bit)'). So \(\rho(q_0)=\kappa\theta_0\), with defect \(e=\kappa\theta_0-\theta_0\) (small; the paper reports a negligible accuracy drop), as for QLoRA. Within the slice at \(\kappa\theta_0\) the trainable block (biases, pretrained lite residuals, head) is regular.

methods.categorical_reading: TinyTL picks its coordinate block by the backprop cone rather than by parameter count. Biases need no stored activation (Obs IV.4), and the lite residual branches see downsampled, narrow activations. As an object it is BitFit \(\oplus\) a selective block of small pretrained branches \(\oplus\) the head.

obstructions.reason: The lite-residual weights add dimensions outside the bias space: \(d(\mathrm{TinyTL})>d(\mathrm{BitFit})\).

Both target activation memory, but LST's side network is an unpointed extension: its initial realisation is not the frozen network's. TinyTL is a coordinate block of the pretrained network pointed at \(\kappa\theta_0\) (the 8-bit base), so the base points differ and no pointed arrow exists.

coord_notes.kind: Discrete trigger tokens placed by a template around the input. The template itself changes the input, so no choice of triggers reproduces \(f\).
coord_notes.shape: \(Q=\mathcal V^\ell\) is finite, so \(d(M)=0\): a finite subset of the vocabulary lattice \(\{E_w\}^\ell\) on the input wire. Function-level relative to \(\Theta\).
coord_notes.base_point: Triggers start at [MASK], and the template already moves the output.
coord_notes.gauge: \(Q\) is discrete: no continuous fibre.
coord_notes.covariance: The candidate set is the rows of the embedding matrix, which move with every linear change of the embedding basis. On the vocabulary side only token permutations act.
coord_notes.merge: Trigger tokens lengthen every input.

methods.categorical_reading: AutoPrompt is prompt tuning restricted to the vocabulary lattice: a 0-dimensional object whose points map into prompt tuning's \(Q\) by \(w\mapsto E_w\). Its HotFlip search ranks swaps by the first-order term \(E_w^\top\nabla\). It uses the cotangent of the continuous relaxation to move on a discrete set.

arrows.note: A smooth map from the finite set \(\mathcal V^\ell\) into prompt tuning at the template's trigger slots, pointed at \(h([\mathrm{MASK}]^\ell)\): a monomorphism of the unpointed slice.

obstructions.reason: BBT reaches the random affine subspace \(p_0+\mathrm{col}A\) of dimension \(k\ll\ell d\). Apart from \(p_0\) itself (when \(p_0\) is drawn from the vocabulary), it generically contains no tuple of vocabulary rows, which are exactly AutoPrompt's points.
